paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it. Moses says the LORD is near to His people whenever they call on Him (Deuteronomy 4:7), and the LORD has spoken to them and shown who He is. So the call is simple: keep His commands, don't add to them or subtract from them (Deuteronomy 4:2), and don't swap Him for anything made with human hands. At Horeb they heard a voice and saw no form (Deuteronomy 4:12), so nothing you can carve or build gets to stand in for Him.

Now, Moses knows we forget, and I get it. I once lost my own name in the back of a drawer. That's why he says to be on guard so the things you've seen don't slip from your heart, and to teach them to your children and grandchildren (Deuteronomy 4:9). He also says the LORD is "a consuming fire, a jealous God" (Deuteronomy 4:24). That tells us how seriously He takes being first in our lives, and it tells us the LORD wants all of us, not a little corner of us.

But listen to the best part, because it's LOUD good news. Even if they scatter, Moses says, "you will find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deuteronomy 4:29). "For the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon you or destroy you or forget the covenant with your fathers" (Deuteronomy 4:31). So, baker, keep Him first, keep His Word close, and if you drift, run back to Him, because He is merciful and He is near. This sermon isn't the end of Moses' words to Israel, and there's more teaching still to come.
